description: Complete redesign of species detail pages (src/species-page.js + src/species-page.css + all species/*.html) with light aesthetic, comic-strip animated storyline, cited data with sources, species photographs, scrollytelling essence, and smooth animations. Also update all 10 public/data/*.json files to add data_sources citations and photo URLs.
steps: STEP 1 - Update all 10 public/data/*.json files: (a) Add 'data_sources' field with structured citations for every statistic: population estimate source, IUCN assessment year, habitat loss figures with source and year. (b) Add 'interesting_facts' array with 3-5 cited fascinating facts per species. (c) Add 'photos' array with Wikimedia Commons or Unsplash URLs for each species (use direct URLs to free high-quality wildlife images - at least 2-3 per species). For photos, use URLs like: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/... for known free images of each species. Include attribution info. (d) Remove 'methodology_notes' field if still present after FEAT-001. Tiger data example structure for data_sources: {"population": {"value": "~4,500", "source": "Global Tiger Initiative", "year": 2023, "url": "https://globaltigerinitiative.org"}, "iucn_status": {"status": "Endangered", "source": "IUCN Red List", "assessed": 2022}, "habitat_loss": {"value": "95% of historical range lost", "source": "WWF", "year": 2023}}

STEP 2 - Rewrite src/species-page.css completely: Change from dark to light dreamy aesthetic. Background: #fafaf8. Text: #1a1a1a. Cards/panels: white with soft shadows and rounded corners. Frosted glass nav bar (light). Remove film grain overlay. Add comic-strip panel styles: .comic-panel with clip-path reveals, border-radius, shadow, sequential layout. Add parallax image styles. Add smooth spring animation keyframes. Add full-bleed photo section styles. Keep responsive breakpoints. Add styles for cited data display (small source text below stats).

STEP 3 - Rewrite src/species-page.js completely: (a) Import and init Lenis for smooth scrolling on species pages too. (b) Redesign renderHero: full-bleed hero image with species photo, light gradient overlay (white not black), floating title with glassmorphism. (c) Add renderComicStrip function: 4 panels that reveal sequentially on scroll (Panel 1: species in habitat with photo, Panel 2: the threat with data viz, Panel 3: media representation with film posters, Panel 4: conservation outcome). Use GSAP ScrollTrigger with scrub for panel reveals. CSS clip-path animations for panel transitions. (d) Redesign renderScience to show ALL data with inline citations - every stat shows '(Source: X, Year)' next to it. Population with source and year. IUCN status with assessment year. (e) Add renderPhotos function: full-width photo gallery section with parallax scrolling images from the photos array in JSON. Include photographer attribution. (f) Add renderInterestingFacts: animated fact cards that float in on scroll, each with citation. (g) Keep renderOnScreen (media cards) but restyle for light theme. Add species photos as hero images in between sections. (h) Remove renderMethodology entirely (already removed in FEAT-001 but ensure species-page.js is clean). (i) Add smooth GSAP ScrollTrigger animations with spring physics for all section reveals. (j) Update renderFooter to light theme.

STEP 4 - Update all 10 species/*.html pages: Ensure they link to the updated species-page.js. Light-themed noscript fallback. Update meta descriptions. No changes to the data-species attribute pattern.
STEP 5 - Run npm run build to verify everything compiles correctly with the new species page code.
acceptance_criteria: All 10 public/data/*.json files have 'data_sources' field with structured citations
All 10 JSON files have 'interesting_facts' array with at least 3 cited facts each
All 10 JSON files have 'photos' array with at least 2 photo objects each (url + attribution)
src/species-page.css has no dark background colors (#0a0a0f)
src/species-page.js includes a comic-strip/storyline rendering function
Every rendered statistic includes a visible source citation
No references to research questions remain in species-page.js
verification: Run: npm run build in /projects/sandbox/species-on-screen -- should exit 0
Run: grep -l 'data_sources' public/data/*.json | wc -l -- should output 10
Run: grep -l 'interesting_facts' public/data/*.json | wc -l -- should output 10
Run: grep -l 'photos' public/data/*.json | wc -l -- should output 10
findings: All verification checks pass. Build succeeds with no errors. All 10 JSON files have data_sources, interesting_facts, and photos fields. species-page.css uses light theme (#fafaf8 background, no dark colors). species-page.js imports Lenis, has renderComicStrip function, and includes inline citations. No RQ references remain. The chunk size warning for main.js (548KB) is pre-existing from Three.js and unrelated to this feature.
